concept.title: Embedded objects (video, audio, documents)
concept.abstract: This section covers Embedded Objects — binary or linked media items that supplement text-based content with demonstrations, walkthroughs, and supporting reference documents — and three scenarios: a video embedded between paragraphs, an audio file embedded between paragraphs, and a PDF, Word, or Excel document embedded between paragraphs. The converter behavior for each depends on the object type and whether it is embedded or linked.

conbody.p: Embedded objects are binary or linked media items — video files, audio recordings, or document attachments. These supplements text-based content with demonstrations, walkthroughs, recorded explanations, and supporting reference documents that cannot be fully expressed as prose or static images.
These objects are stored using one of two mechanisms:

ul.li: OLE (Object Linking and Embedding) binary containers, where the object data is fully enclosed in the document archive.
Linked references, where only the file path URL is stored and the actual object data is external.

conbody.note: If your Markdown uses raw HTML or custom extensions such as Sphinx roles, MkDocs admonitions, GitHub-style callouts, share syntax samples with the DITA architecture team so the Markdown converter configuration can be customized.
